Leona.build: Swain has no escape ability, so consider tenacity first if Leona’s chain crowd control is a problem. Choose resistances based on the type of damage dealt by the enemy damage dealers while Leona holds you in place; magic resistance is effective against Leona’s own magic damage.
Leona.combo: While Leona E Zenith Blade is down, place Swain W Vision of Empire along the movement path in advance to apply a slow. Then root the target with Swain E Nevermove, recast it to pull them in, and hit them with Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. In fights with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, use the attack that becomes available again after you’ve drained and healed enough.
Leona.escape: Right after you bait Leona into using Leona E Zenith Blade, Swain has a window to close the distance. Land Swain E Nevermove to root a target, while staying alert to the range at which Leona can engage with Leona Q Shield of Daybreak.
Leona.fight: Keep your distance until Leona E Zenith Blade is down. Catch Leona with Swain E Nevermove and retaliate right after she uses it. Swain Q Death's Hand is stronger at close range after pulling her in than as a poke from maximum range.
Leona.laning: Leona E Zenith Blade pierces in a straight line, so don’t stand in line with your allied ranged carry. Use Swain E Nevermove to stop enemies from approaching the wave, but don’t push while it’s down. Use Swain Q Death's Hand to hit the enemy ranged carry along with the wave when they step up to last-hit.
Leona.phase: If you avoid falling far behind early and build up Soul Fragments, the game becomes more favorable for Swain as it goes on.
Leona.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull someone in with Swain E Nevermove. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy groups up and moves in, so it reaches multiple targets. If you receive Leona P Sunlight’s mark, immediately back away to avoid the enemy’s follow-up damage.
Leona.watch: If Leona E Zenith Blade hits you, she dashes in and can follow with the stun from Leona Q Shield of Daybreak, so don’t give her room to engage. When Leona activates Leona W Eclipse, move out of its area before it explodes. When the marker for Leona R Solar Flare appears, move sideways to avoid the stun in the center.

Maokai.fight: Move forward and trade right after Maokai W Twisted Advance is down. Don’t use abilities on Maokai while he is dashing; catch him with Swain E Nevermove after he lands. Hitting Maokai with abilities makes Maokai P Sap Magic’s healing come back sooner, so focus your poke on the enemy damage dealer.
Maokai.build: Get movement speed first so you can escape Maokai’s telegraphed attack areas. Magic resistance counters Maokai’s damage, but choose your actual resistance based on the enemy damage dealer who attacks while Maokai holds you in place. Also consider tenacity against the roots from Maokai W Twisted Advance and Maokai R Nature's Grasp.
Maokai.combo: After Maokai W Twisted Advance is down, place Swain W Vision of Empire along the enemy damage dealer’s path in advance. Hit the slowed target with Swain E Nevermove, recast it to pull them in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. If Maokai is dashing, save your abilities until he lands.
Maokai.escape: Right after Maokai W Twisted Advance is used, Swain has a window to close the distance. After the dash ends, catch Maokai with Swain E Nevermove so he can’t get away.
Maokai.laning: Early on, watch the range of Maokai W Twisted Advance and focus on avoiding a major disadvantage. Pressure the enemy damage dealer with Swain E Nevermove, but don’t push while it’s down. After leveling up Swain Q Death's Hand, hit the enemy damage dealer and the wave together when they step up to last-hit.
Maokai.phase: Swain has limited mana early, and being caught by Maokai is dangerous, so play safely and endure. Later, the more stacks Swain builds with Swain P Ravenous Flock, the more favorable things become for Swain.
Maokai.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull an enemy in with Swain E Nevermove. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension where it will hit multiple targets when the enemy groups up and moves in. Fight in open terrain where there’s room to dodge Maokai R Nature's Grasp.
Maokai.watch: If caught by Maokai W Twisted Advance, Swain has no escape ability and can easily be hit by follow-up attacks. Don’t give Maokai room to engage near bushes while Maokai W Twisted Advance is available. Watch out for Maokai E Sapling Toss from bushes, and if Maokai R Nature's Grasp comes from a distance, move perpendicular to its direction.

Alistar.teamfight: Stay just behind your team’s frontline and pull one target with Swain E Nevermove. While Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don’t spend your damage on Alistar; target the damage dealers behind him. If you can’t retreat, interrupt Alistar’s engage with Swain E Nevermove after he activates R, then activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemies group up and engage.
Alistar.combo: After Alistar’s engage abilities are used, place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on the enemy’s path, then hit the slowed target with Swain E Nevermove. Recast E to pull them in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. When fighting with Swain R Demonic Ascension, hold the enemy with E to keep draining and healing, and don’t recast R as soon as it becomes available.
Alistar.laning: Keep your distance early and avoid Alistar’s engage. Hit a champion with Swain E Nevermove to pressure them away from the wave, but don’t push the lane while E is down. When the enemy marksman steps up to last-hit, harass them along with the wave using Swain Q Death's Hand.
Alistar.phase: Early on, Swain lacks mana and an escape, so keep your distance and avoid falling far behind Alistar. As you gain health from Soul Fragments, the matchup becomes more favorable for Swain.
Alistar.build: Consider prioritizing tenacity, since Alistar’s crowd control can leave you locked down and killed. Build magic resistance against the damage from Alistar Q Pulverize, Alistar W Headbutt, and Alistar E Trample.
Alistar.escape: The moment after Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are used is your window to move forward. In particular, if you bait out Alistar W Headbutt and then hit him with Swain E Nevermove, it will be difficult for Alistar to get away.
Alistar.fight: Take your position and counterattack just after Alistar Q Pulverize and Alistar W Headbutt are used. When Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, back off instead of committing your damage, then fight again after it ends.
Alistar.watch: Watch for Alistar W Headbutt to close the distance, followed by Alistar Q Pulverize and Alistar E Trample to lock you down. Swain has no escape, so keep your distance while both abilities are available. Near a turret, don’t give Alistar room to circle behind you.

Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns if it hits a wall or a second target, so don’t stand with your back to a wall or in a line with an ally or minion. Watch for Bard E Magical Journey to flank you, and don’t rush your attack before Bard R Tempered Fate’s damage immunity ends.
Bard.build: Prioritize tenacity to prepare for being focused after Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns you. Bard deals magic damage, so build magic resistance afterward; armor is not a priority.
Bard.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on Bard’s path to slow him, then root him with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. In a fight with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, keep your target in range with roots and pulls to continue draining, then recast after you’ve gotten enough drain and healing.
Bard.escape: Right after Bard E Magical Journey is used, Bard has no escape, so close the distance and catch him with Swain E Nevermove. If Bard Q Cosmic Binding is also down, you have an opening to engage without needing to dodge its stun.
Bard.fight: Bait out Bard E Magical Journey, then catch him with Swain E Nevermove to create an opening to engage. Use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range on a target you’ve pulled rather than to harass from afar. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you can hold the enemy with Swain E Nevermove or an ally’s crowd control.
Bard.laning: If Bard W Caretaker's Shrine is visible in lane, walk over it to remove it. Use Swain E Nevermove to pressure the enemy away from the wave, but don’t push the lane while that ability is down.
Bard.phase: Early on, Swain lacks the mana for repeated fights, so avoid them and focus on not falling far behind. Swain’s health increases as you collect Soul Fragments, so the matchup becomes more favorable over time.
Bard.teamfight: Stay just behind your team’s frontline and pull one target with Swain E Nevermove. When the enemies move in together and you can reach multiple targets, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension to keep draining and healing. Targets caught by Bard R Tempered Fate are immune to damage, so time your attack for when that effect ends.

Lulu.escape: When Lulu W Whimsy has been used on another ally, that’s your chance to engage. Lulu has no dash, so limit her path with Swain W Vision of Empire and catch her with Swain E Nevermove.
Lulu.build: The provided information isn’t enough to determine a first purchase. Magic resistance is more useful than armor against Lulu’s damage, but Lulu herself deals little damage, so choose resistances based on the damage type of the target she protects. Also consider movement speed to leave telegraphed areas and tenacity to reduce the disruption from Lulu W Whimsy and Lulu R Wild Growth.
Lulu.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire along Lulu’s path first, then hit the slowed Lulu with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. If Swain R Demonic Ascension is active in a teamfight, hold enemies with Swain E Nevermove to drain and heal, then use Swain R Demonic Ascension again when it becomes available.
Lulu.fight: Place Swain W Vision of Empire along Lulu’s path in advance to slow her, then hit her with Swain E Nevermove. Lulu is strong in all-in fights, so poke steadily in normal situations.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the extra damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion. Whenever possible, hit champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to build Soul Fragments and pressure their approach to the lane. Don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down, and focus on pressuring the lane and maintaining river vision instead of roaming.
Lulu.phase: Swain has limited mana early, so avoid repeated fights and manage your distance while enduring Lulu’s poke. Each Soul Fragment increases Swain’s maximum health, so the game becomes more favorable later if you avoid falling far behind early.
Lulu.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch someone with Swain E Nevermove, pulling them in if you need to move them toward your team. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy groups up and moves in, so it reaches multiple targets and keeps you draining and healing. If Lulu R Wild Growth is available, target Lulu herself or someone else instead of the ally she is protecting.
Lulu.watch: Lulu W Whimsy prevents Swain from using abilities and attacks, so don’t force an engage while Lulu W Whimsy is available. Manage your distance to avoid the slow from Lulu Q Glitterlance. Lulu R Wild Growth knocks up nearby enemies and instantly increases its target’s health, so don’t count on killing a protected target while Lulu R Wild Growth is available.

Ashe.build: Ashe deals mostly physical damage, and Swain has relatively low armor, so build armor first. Buy Cloth Armor early and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots.
Ashe.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on Ashe’s path to slow her, then root her with Swain E Nevermove. Recast E to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. Even in a fight with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, hold Ashe with Swain E Nevermove to get as much drain and healing as possible before recasting Swain R Demonic Ascension.
Ashe.escape: Right after Ashe W Volley is used is your chance to engage with Swain E Nevermove. Swain has no mobility, so don’t try to walk through Ashe’s basic attack slows; catch her first with Swain E Nevermove.
Ashe.fight: Trade after Ashe W Volley is used and Ashe Q Ranger's Focus ends. Place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead so Ashe has less room to dodge by changing direction, then catch the slowed Ashe with Swain E Nevermove.
Ashe.laning: Early on, focus on holding your ground without staying exposed to Ashe’s slow for long, and look to land Swain E Nevermove at maximum range. When Ashe steps up to last-hit, hit both her and the wave with Swain Q Death's Hand. While Swain E Nevermove is down, you have no way to intervene, so don’t push the lane. Hit champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to gain growth stacks.
Ashe.phase: Early on, Swain lacks the mana for repeated fights and is easily caught by Ashe’s slows, so focus on holding your ground. If you avoid falling far behind early and collect Soul Fragments, Swain’s health will grow and the matchup will become more favorable over time.
Ashe.teamfight: Stay just behind your team’s frontline and look for an angle to pull Ashe with Swain E Nevermove. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemies move in together and you can reach multiple targets, then recast it after getting your drain and healing. Swain has no mobility, so don’t walk in first.
Ashe.watch: Dodge to the side of Ashe W Volley’s cone, since it harasses with an area slow, and look to trade right after it is used. Ashe P Frost Shot refreshes its slow with each basic attack, so don’t stay within Ashe’s attack range for long. When Ashe Q Ranger's Focus is active, create distance. While Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow is available, don’t start a small skirmish from out of vision.

Blitzcrank.build: Swain has no mobility, so chained crowd control is especially dangerous; consider prioritizing tenacity. Build magic resistance against the damage from Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field. Blitzcrank R Static Field destroys shields, so relying on shields to survive is less effective.
Blitzcrank.combo: When Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses, place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on the enemy’s path, then hit the slowed target with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull them in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. In a fight with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, hold your target for draining with roots and pulls, then recast Swain R Demonic Ascension after getting enough healing.
Blitzcrank.escape: The moment Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses is your chance to move forward. If you catch him with Swain E Nevermove then, it will be difficult for him to get away since he has no ability to create distance. Don’t close the distance first while Blitzcrank still has crowd control available.
Blitzcrank.fight: Trade right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses. Place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on the enemy’s path to slow them, hit with Swain E Nevermove, then pull them in and use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range.
Blitzcrank.laning: Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls only the first target it hits, so don’t stand beside minions; always stand behind them. If the grab misses, gain an advantage by pushing the lane or trading, but don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down. Use Swain W Vision of Empire to check bushes, and keep an eye on Blitzcrank’s mana.
Blitzcrank.phase: Early on, Swain lacks the mana for repeated fights, so hold your ground while dodging Blitzcrank’s grabs. Your maximum health increases as you collect Soul Fragments, so the matchup becomes more favorable later if you avoid falling far behind early.
Blitzcrank.teamfight: Stay just behind your team’s frontline and pull one target with Swain E Nevermove. Avoid walking into a position where Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab can catch you.
Blitzcrank.watch: If Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab catches you, Blitzcrank can follow with the knockup from Blitzcrank E Power Fist and the silence from Blitzcrank R Static Field. Swain has no way to escape, so stand behind minions and keep away from bushes when you don’t have vision of them.

Brand.build: Brand deals magic damage, and Brand P Blaze deals damage based on your maximum health, so build magic resistance first. Also get movement speed to help you leave telegraphed areas.
Brand.combo: After Brand W Pillar of Flame is used, place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on Brand’s path. Hit the slowed Brand with Swain E Nevermove and recast it to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. When fighting with Swain R Demonic Ascension, activate it when you can hold Brand, then recast it after getting enough drain and healing.
Brand.escape: The moment Brand W Pillar of Flame is used is your chance to engage. If you aren’t ablaze, Brand Q Sear won’t stun you even if it hits, so close the distance with Swain E Nevermove to keep Brand from getting away.
Brand.fight: Close the distance after Brand W Pillar of Flame is used, as long as you aren’t ablaze. Brand has no mobility, so block his path with Swain W Vision of Empire and catch him with Swain E Nevermove at maximum range.
Brand.laning: Early on, dodge Brand’s first ability and hold your ground without taking heavy losses. Don’t last-hit beside burning minions. When the enemy steps up to last-hit, hit both them and the wave with Swain Q Death's Hand. Use Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove on champions to gain Soul Fragments and lane pressure.
Brand.phase: Early on, Swain lacks the mana to trade repeatedly, so hold your ground while avoiding Brand’s harassment. Swain’s maximum health increases as you collect Soul Fragments, so the matchup becomes more favorable later if you avoid falling far behind early.
Brand.teamfight: Keep your distance from allies to reduce the spread of Brand E Conflagration and the bounces of Brand R Pyroclasm, and don’t stand beside an ally who is ablaze. Stay just behind your team’s frontline and pull one target with Swain E Nevermove. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemies move in together and you can reach multiple targets.
Brand.watch: If Brand W Pillar of Flame or Brand Q Sear hits you first, Brand P Blaze can apply its stacks, so dodge his first ability. If you’re ablaze, move out of the projectile’s path or hide behind a minion to avoid the stun from Brand Q Sear. Be wary of Brand E Conflagration spreading near burning minions.

Braum.build: Swain has no escape and is vulnerable to Braum’s chained crowd control, so prioritize tenacity. If you build resistances, choose magic resistance to match Braum’s main damage.
Braum.combo: After Braum E Unbreakable’s shield drops, or from the side it isn’t facing, place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on the enemy’s path. Hit the slowed target with Swain E Nevermove at maximum range and recast it to pull them in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. In a fight with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, catch and pull them with E, then recast R after getting enough drain and healing.
Braum.escape: The moment after Braum W Stand Behind Me is used is your window to catch him with Swain E Nevermove. Keep your distance and don’t engage first while Braum still has crowd control available.
Braum.fight: Keep your distance and bait out Braum W Stand Behind Me, then look for a chance to catch him with Swain E Nevermove. Place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on his path to slow him, hit him with Swain E Nevermove, then pull him in and use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you have a way to hold the enemy and can keep reaching them.
Braum.laning: Stand behind minions to block Braum Q Winter's Bite, but avoid positions where there’s a gap between minions and you’re directly in line with Braum. Use Swain E Nevermove to pressure the enemy away from the wave, and don’t push while E is down.
Braum.phase: Early on, Swain lacks mana and escape tools, so hold your ground while avoiding Braum’s mark and chained crowd control. In the late game, you’ll be more durable with the health gained from Soul Fragments.
Braum.teamfight: Stay just behind your team’s frontline and pull one target with Swain E Nevermove, while finding an angle that avoids the front of Braum E Unbreakable. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemies move in together and you can reach multiple targets. Dodge the straight path of Braum R Glacial Fissure, and target the person Braum is protecting instead of focusing your damage on Braum.
Braum.watch: Braum Q Winter's Bite hits only the first target, so stand behind minions. If Braum P Concussive Blows marks you, get out of range before you’re stunned. When facing Braum E Unbreakable, wait for the shield to drop or find an angle from the side. If you see Braum R Glacial Fissure’s cast animation, dodge its straight path to the side and avoid the remaining slow zone as well.

Heimerdinger.build: Prioritize movement speed so you can get out of telegraphed attack areas. If you build resistances, choose magic resistance, which helps against the damage from Heimerdinger’s turrets, rockets, and grenades. Since Swain can’t dodge with mobility, tenacity is also worth considering to reduce the stun from the center of the grenade.
Heimerdinger.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on Heimerdinger’s path, then hit the slowed target with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. If you activate Swain R Demonic Ascension, recast it after getting enough drain and healing.
Heimerdinger.escape: Root and pull with Swain E Nevermove, but if you’re hit by a grenade, stop your engage and first get out of turret range.
Heimerdinger.fight: Don’t repeatedly trade head-on with the turrets; target Heimerdinger from the side or from a bush. Block his path with Swain W Vision of Empire and close the distance by hitting him with Swain E Nevermove.
Heimerdinger.laning: Early on, don’t force fights in front of Heimerdinger’s turret setup. Pressure Heimerdinger himself from an angle where Swain E Nevermove can reach him. Hit champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to collect Soul Fragments. While Swain E Nevermove is down, you have no way to intervene, so don’t push the lane.
Heimerdinger.phase: Early on, Swain lacks mana and escape tools, so hold your ground while avoiding Heimerdinger’s turret setup. In the late game, fight more durably with the health gained from Soul Fragments.
Heimerdinger.teamfight: Stay just behind your team’s frontline and pull Heimerdinger himself or an enemy who engages with Swain E Nevermove. When enemies move in together and you have a way to hold them, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension to drain multiple targets. If Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is still available, don’t group with your allies in a narrow passage or at one spot in front of an objective.
Heimerdinger.watch: When Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, watch for the empowered grenade and rockets, and don’t group up in narrow passages.

Hwei.build: Build magic resistance first to prepare for Hwei’s damage. Even though Swain P Ravenous Flock increases your health, account for the damage based on your maximum health from Hwei Q Subject: Disaster. Also consider movement speed to leave area effects and tenacity against Hwei E Subject: Torment.
Hwei.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on Hwei’s path to slow him. Then root him with Swain E Nevermove, recast it to pull him in, and hit him with Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. If you use Q before pulling him in, it’s difficult to hit him with multiple bolts at once.
Hwei.escape: Engage after Hwei E Subject: Torment is used. Hwei has no mobility, so if you catch him with Swain E Nevermove then, it will be difficult for him to get away. If E is still available and you go in first, he may stop your engage with a root or forced movement.
Hwei.fight: Hwei E Subject: Torment is your chance to close the distance right after he uses it to harass or clear the wave. Hwei W Subject: Serenity can increase his movement speed, so place Swain W Vision of Empire ahead on his path to slow him, then hit him with Swain E Nevermove. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you can catch him with E.
Hwei.laning: Early on, avoid forcing repeated fights. When Hwei steps up to last-hit, attack him along with the wave using Swain Q Death's Hand. Hit Hwei with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to gain Soul Fragments and lane pressure. While E is down, you have no way to intervene, so don’t push the lane.
Hwei.phase: Early on, Swain lacks mana, so focus on not falling far behind. As you collect Soul Fragments with Swain P Ravenous Flock, your health increases and the matchup becomes more favorable over time.
Hwei.teamfight: Stay just behind your team’s frontline and watch for Hwei E Subject: Torment to be used, then pull one target with Swain E Nevermove. When the enemies move in together, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension from a position where you can reach multiple targets and keep draining and healing. Take a wide route instead of entering a narrow passage Hwei has set up.
Hwei.watch: If Hwei E Subject: Torment roots or displaces you, you’re likely to be hit by the follow-up attack too. If the first ability hits, move immediately to avoid the second ability and Hwei P Signature of the Visionary’s explosion. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster also deals damage based on your maximum health, so get out of its telegraphed area.

Janna.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire along the movement path first, then hit the slowed Janna with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. In fights with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, drain and heal enough before using Swain R Demonic Ascension again when it is available to recast.
Janna.escape: After Janna Q Howling Gale is down, you have a chance to land Swain E Nevermove without worrying about being knocked up. If Janna R Monsoon is down, there’s less risk of being pushed away, too. Janna can pass through minions with Janna W Zephyr, so don’t try to block her path; catch her with Swain E Nevermove.
Janna.fight: Engage after Janna wastes Janna Q Howling Gale or uses Janna E Eye Of The Storm. Place Swain W Vision of Empire along Janna’s path to slow her, then hit her with Swain E Nevermove at maximum range and pull her in. If Janna E Eye Of The Storm is on someone else, target Janna.
Janna.laning: Mana is limited early, so avoid forcing repeated fights. Pressure the ally Janna is protecting to make her use Janna E Eye Of The Storm, and bait her into wasting Janna Q Howling Gale and Janna W Zephyr. Use Swain E Nevermove to keep them from approaching the wave, but don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Janna.phase: Swain has limited mana early, so focus on avoiding major losses. Later, Swain becomes tougher as stacks from Swain P Ravenous Flock build up.
Janna.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull someone in with Swain E Nevermove. If Janna is behind her damage dealers stopping an engage, look for the moment she is isolated. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy groups up and moves in, so it reaches multiple targets, and watch out for being pushed away by Janna R Monsoon.
Janna.watch: Janna Q Howling Gale’s knockup is dangerous, so if you hear it charging out of sight, move out of its line. Janna R Monsoon pushes Swain away as he engages, so be ready to use Swain E Nevermove to pull when she casts Janna R Monsoon. Don’t focus damage on a target affected by Janna E Eye Of The Storm until the shield is gone.

Karma.build: Karma’s main damage is magic, so buy magic resistance first. Also get movement speed so you can break Karma W Focused Resolve’s tether and leave ground effects.
Karma.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire along Karma’s path in advance to slow her, then hit her with Swain E Nevermove at maximum range. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range. If Swain R Demonic Ascension is active, hold enemy champions with Swain E Nevermove so you can keep draining them, then use Swain R Demonic Ascension again after draining and healing enough.
Karma.escape: When Karma W Focused Resolve is down, that’s your chance to engage. If a shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra has been applied, wait for its duration to end, then use Swain E Nevermove to catch an opponent.
Karma.fight: Don’t engage first while Karma W Focused Resolve is available; create distance and bait her into using it. After Karma W Focused Resolve is down and the shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra expires, block Karma’s path with Swain W Vision of Empire, then land Swain E Nevermove to start the fight.
Karma.laning: Early on, dodge Karma’s poke and avoid falling far behind. Build stacks by hitting champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove. When an opponent steps forward to last-hit, hit them and the wave together with Swain Q Death's Hand. Don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Karma.phase: Swain has limited mana early, so survive by dodging Karma’s poke. Later, Swain gains an advantage from the health stacked through Swain P Ravenous Flock.
Karma.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch someone with Swain E Nevermove to pull them in. After Karma W Focused Resolve is down and the shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra ends, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension where it will hit multiple targets if the enemy groups up and moves in.
Karma.watch: Karma Q Inner Flame’s area slow is dangerous, so stand behind minions or outside its range to avoid being hit. If you’re hit by the fire field from Karma Q Inner Flame empowered by Karma R Mantra, walk out of the circle before it detonates. If you’re tethered by Karma W Focused Resolve, create distance to break the tether before the root lands.

Lux.build: Get movement speed first so you can escape the area where Lux E Lucent Singularity lands. Build magic resistance against Lux’s damage, and get tenacity as well to reduce the chance of taking follow-up attacks while rooted by Lux Q Light Binding.
Lux.combo: If Lux Q Light Binding misses, place Swain W Vision of Empire along her path and hit the slowed Lux with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range so you can hit her with multiple bolts. In fights with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, keep Lux in range with roots and pulls, then use Swain R Demonic Ascension again after draining and healing enough.
Lux.escape: Engage after dodging Lux Q Light Binding. Lux has no mobility ability to create distance, so close in and catch her with Swain E Nevermove.
Lux.fight: Right after baiting and dodging Lux Q Light Binding, you have a chance to close the distance. Place Swain W Vision of Empire along Lux’s path in advance to slow her, then catch and pull her in with Swain E Nevermove before using Swain Q Death's Hand at close range.
Lux.laning: Early on, Swain has difficulty using Swain E Nevermove repeatedly, so avoid forcing fights. Stand apart laterally from your allies so you aren’t hit together by Lux Q Light Binding. Build Soul Fragments by hitting Lux with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove, and don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Lux.phase: Swain has limited mana early, so avoid repeated fights and focus on dodging Lux Q Light Binding. If you avoid falling far behind early and build Soul Fragments, Swain becomes more favorable as the game goes on.
Lux.teamfight: Approach spread out just behind your frontline so you aren’t all caught by Lux E Lucent Singularity. Pull someone in with Swain E Nevermove, then activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy groups up and moves in, so it reaches multiple targets. If Lux R Final Spark’s targeting line appears while you’re retreating at low health, dodge sideways.
Lux.watch: If Lux Q Light Binding hits you, follow-up abilities will follow, so bait it out and dodge it first. It roots the first two targets hit, so don’t stand in line with an ally. If Lux’s ability hits you, move outside her attack range before Lux P Illumination’s mark is triggered by a basic attack.

Milio.build: Choose your resistance first based on the enemy damage dealer’s damage type. If considering only the damage from Milio P Fired Up! and Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick, magic resistance is effective; if the healing from Milio W Cozy Campfire and Milio R Breath of Life is a problem, get Grievous Wounds.
Milio.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire along Milio’s path first, then hit the slowed Milio with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range.
Milio.escape: Right after Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is used, you have a chance to close the distance. Milio has no mobility ability, so catch him with Swain E Nevermove then, but only activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you have a way to hold him in place.
Milio.fight: Look for an angle to catch Milio with Swain E Nevermove after Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down. Place Swain W Vision of Empire along the movement path in advance and start the trade after it applies a slow, then pull the target in with Swain E Nevermove and use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range.
Milio.laning: Early on, conserve mana while hitting champions with Swain E Nevermove and Swain W Vision of Empire to build Soul Fragments. After leveling up Swain Q Death's Hand, hit the enemy ranged carry and the wave together when they step up to last-hit, and don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Milio.phase: Swain has limited mana early, so build up Swain P Ravenous Flock stacks while avoiding major losses. Swain gains health from Soul Fragments later, but Milio’s team also gets stronger over time, so secure lane priority during the laning phase.
Milio.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull someone in with Swain E Nevermove. If you can catch Milio, prioritize him, as he has low health and defensive stats. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy groups up and moves in and it can reach multiple targets, then finish the fight after healing enough.
Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is his only disengage tool and knocks back the first enemy it hits, so don’t force an engage while it’s available. When Milio W Cozy Campfire is active and increases the enemy ranged carry’s range, delay the frontline fight and let its duration run out.

Morgana.build: Build magic resistance first against Morgana’s main damage. Swain has no escape ability, so it’s difficult to get away after being caught by Morgana Q Dark Binding and R Soul Shackles; consider tenacity first if crowd control is a bigger problem. If a long duel makes Morgana’s healing a problem, consider Grievous Wounds.
Morgana.combo: When Morgana E Black Shield is down, place Swain W Vision of Empire along her path first, then hit the slowed Morgana with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death's Hand at close range.
Morgana.escape: Engage with Swain E Nevermove while Morgana E Black Shield is down. If you have dodged Morgana Q Dark Binding, the risk of being caught is lower, and Morgana has no ability to create distance on her own, making it difficult for her to escape Swain once he closes in.
Morgana.fight: Manage your distance behind minions so you can dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding, then fight after Morgana E Black Shield is down. Place Swain W Vision of Empire along Morgana’s path to slow her, then catch her with Swain E Nevermove. Use Swain Q Death's Hand after pulling her in and closing the distance.
Morgana.laning: Early on, Swain has difficulty using Swain E Nevermove repeatedly, so survive while dodging Morgana Q Dark Binding. When an opponent steps forward to last-hit, use Swain Q Death's Hand to hit them and the wave together, and use Swain E Nevermove to pressure their approach to the wave. Don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Morgana.phase: Swain has limited mana early, so focus on dodging Morgana Q Dark Binding and avoiding a major disadvantage. As Soul Fragments build up, Swain’s maximum health increases, helping him stay strong in the late game.
Morgana.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull someone in with Swain E Nevermove. Don’t waste crowd control on a target protected by Morgana E Black Shield. If the enemy groups up and moves in, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension where it will hit multiple targets and keep draining and healing.
Morgana.watch: Morgana Q Dark Binding catches only the first target it hits, so move with a minion between you and her. If it hits, Morgana W Tormented Shadow and follow-up attacks will follow; the lower the health, the more dangerous the W field becomes, so avoid it while retreating. Morgana R Soul Shackles stuns after a delay, so move outside its range when you see the chains.

Nami.build: Counter the healing from Nami W Ebb and Flow by prioritizing healing reduction with Morellonomicon. Build magic resistance rather than armor to defend against Nami’s damage.
Nami.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Nami’s path to slow her, then hit Swain E Nevermove near its maximum range. Recast E to pull Nami in and hit her with Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. When fighting with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, catch Nami with E to maintain your drain, and recast R only after you’ve healed enough.
Nami.escape: Immediately after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses, you have an opening to engage. Wait until Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing has also expired, then catch Nami with Swain E Nevermove as she is slowed by Swain W Vision of Empire.
Nami.fight: Target Nami immediately after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses. Place Swain W Vision of Empire in her path to slow her, then catch her with Swain E Nevermove and pull her close before using Swain Q Death’s Hand. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you can catch her with E to keep draining and healing.
Nami.laning: Early on, avoid repeated fights because of the mana cost of Swain E Nevermove. Hit Nami with E to pressure her, and when the enemy ranged carry steps up to last-hit, use Swain Q Death’s Hand to hit both the wave and your opponent. Don’t push while E is down, since you have no way to intervene.
Nami.phase: Swain is mana-starved early, so focus on avoiding Nami’s crowd control and not falling far behind. Later, the bonus health from soul fragments collected with Swain P Ravenous Flock becomes powerful.
Nami.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove to pull them in. When the enemy groups up and moves in and Swain R Demonic Ascension can hit multiple targets, activate R and recast it after draining and healing enough. If you see Nami R Tidal Wave, sidestep first to avoid the follow-up Nami Q Aqua Prison combo.
Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison sets up follow-up attacks with a stun, so sidestep when you see it coming. Nami R Tidal Wave travels slowly, but getting hit lets her continue the combo, so move sideways as soon as you see it. Don’t fight head-on against a target affected by Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing; wait for the effect to end, then look for another opening.

Nautilus.build: Build magic resistance first against the damage from Nautilus Q Dredge Line, W Titan’s Wrath, and E Riptide. Since Swain has no escape and can easily die while locked down by crowd control, you can prioritize tenacity over magic resistance.
Nautilus.combo: Once Nautilus Q Dredge Line is down, place Swain W Vision of Empire in your opponent’s path. Hit the slowed target with Swain E Nevermove and pull them in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand when they are close. When fighting with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, recast it after draining and healing as much as possible.
Nautilus.escape: Immediately after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses, Swain has a chance to close the gap and catch a target with Swain E Nevermove. Swain has no escape, so don’t move in first while Nautilus Q Dredge Line is available.
Nautilus.fight: Trade immediately after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses. Place Swain W Vision of Empire along the movement path to apply a slow, land Swain E Nevermove, then pull the target in and use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range.
Nautilus.laning: Keep your distance and hold your ground early, using Swain E Nevermove to pressure your opponent’s approach to the wave. Don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down. When the enemy ranged carry steps up to last-hit, use Swain Q Death’s Hand to hit them along with the wave.
Nautilus.phase: Early on, watch out for Nautilus’s chain of crowd control and focus on not falling far behind. The more soul fragments you collect, the higher your maximum health, giving you an advantage as the game goes on.
Nautilus.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull an enemy in with Swain E Nevermove. When the enemy groups up and moves in and Swain R Demonic Ascension can hit multiple targets, activate R. Don’t line up with an ally along the path of Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Nautilus.watch: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits you, he can follow up with more crowd control, so keep minions between you and him. Don’t linger within range of Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s basic attack, and when Nautilus R Depth Charge is available, avoid lining up with an ally along its path.

Neeko.build: Build magic resistance first against Neeko’s main damage. If you die after being hit by Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and then Neeko R Pop Blossom, prioritize tenacity. Movement speed also helps you leave the marked area.
Neeko.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Neeko’s path to slow her, then hit her with Swain E Nevermove. Recast E to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. It’s hard to hit multiple bolts with Q if you cast it first from far away.
Neeko.escape: Immediately after Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down, you have a chance to close in and force a trade.
Neeko.fight: Swain has no escape, so manage your distance while Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is available. Once Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or Neeko R Pop Blossom is down, slow her path with Swain W Vision of Empire and engage by catching her with Swain E Nevermove.
Neeko.laning: Avoid forcing repeated fights early, and look for chances to hit both Neeko and the wave with Swain Q Death’s Hand after leveling it up. Pressure her approach to the lane with Swain E Nevermove, but don’t push while E is down. Hit Neeko with Swain W Vision of Empire and E to collect soul fragments.
Neeko.phase: Swain is mana-starved early and has difficulty fighting repeatedly, so focus on not falling far behind. Later, Swain gains value as his soul fragments build up his health.
Neeko.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove to pull them in. Since Neeko can approach while disguised, spread out from your allies when someone suspicious gets close to avoid Neeko R Pop Blossom. When enemies move in as a group and you have a way to catch them, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension to drain multiple targets.
Neeko.watch: Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and speeds up if it hits something first, so don’t stand in line with an ally. If Neeko approaches while disguised, you may not see the windup for Neeko R Pop Blossom; spread out as soon as someone suspicious gets close. Don’t chase Neeko W Shapesplitter’s clone.

Pantheon.build: Use Cloth Armor to survive early and buy Plated Steelcaps. Pantheon’s main damage is physical, so build armor first, but don’t rely on stacking health alone because Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on your maximum health. Get Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier if an engaging damage dealer can quickly burst Swain down.
Pantheon.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Pantheon’s path to slow him, then root him with Swain E Nevermove. Recast E to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand when he is close. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault is blocking you from the front, wait for it to end or attack from the side.
Pantheon.escape: The window after Pantheon W Shield Vault is down and before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back is a chance to engage. Pantheon can use multiple movement abilities to escape, so don’t force an engage just because one is down. Use that window to catch him with Swain E Nevermove.
Pantheon.fight: Don’t attack Pantheon from the front while Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active; wait for it to end or angle in from the side. Catch him with Swain E Nevermove, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range.
Pantheon.laning: Survive without giving up early kills, and hit champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to build scaling stacks. Don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down, since you have no way to engage. Swain has no mobility or escape, so keep pressure in lane and limit your movement to things like maintaining river vision.
Pantheon.phase: As Swain collects soul fragments, he becomes tougher, while Pantheon’s impact falls off later in the game. Survive the early game and buy time.
Pantheon.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove to pull them in. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy moves in as a group, you can hit multiple targets, and you have a way to catch them. While Pantheon E Aegis Assault blocks attacks from the front, angle your attack from the side or wait for it to end.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault targets and stuns you, so don’t let him get in jump range. When Pantheon Q Comet Spear is used at long range to poke, keep minions between you and him. Walk out of the landing area when you see the warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall.

Pyke.build: Use Cloth Armor to survive early and buy Plated Steelcaps. Pyke’s damage is mostly physical, so build armor first. Against Pyke as he stacks penetration, also get health to stay above the execute threshold for Pyke R Death From Below.
Pyke.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Pyke’s path to slow him, then root him with Swain E Nevermove. Recast E to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand when he is close.
Pyke.escape: Immediately after dodging the stun from Pyke E Phantom Undertow, you have a chance to catch him with Swain E Nevermove. If Pyke R Death From Below has also been spent and has not come back yet, look to engage during the window when all of Pyke’s movement abilities are down.
Pyke.fight: Keep your distance to avoid getting hit by Pyke Q Bone Skewer and then Pyke E Phantom Undertow in succession, and be cautious about early trades. After dodging Pyke E Phantom Undertow, slow his path with Swain W Vision of Empire and catch him with Swain E Nevermove to trade. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you can catch Pyke with Swain E Nevermove or an ally’s crowd control.
Pyke.laning: Aim Swain E Nevermove at Pyke from maximum range, and if it hits, pull him in to collect a soul fragment. Don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down, since you have no way to engage. If Pyke retreats after a trade, maintain vision to prevent healing from Pyke P Gift of the Drowned Ones, and use Swain W Vision of Empire to check bushes and approach paths.
Pyke.phase: Swain is mana-starved early, and Pyke can easily follow up if he catches you, so keep your distance and use Cloth Armor to survive. Later, fight with the health gained from soul fragments, but watch your health so it doesn’t fall below Pyke R Death From Below’s execute threshold.
Pyke.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove. When the enemy moves in as a group, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension from a position where it can hit multiple targets. Don’t stand beside low-health allies and risk both of you being hit by Pyke R Death From Below’s X-shaped area. Keep squishy allies behind the frontline as you move together, and look for a chance to catch Pyke while Pyke E Phantom Undertow is down.
Pyke.watch: If Pyke Q Bone Skewer pulls you in, he can easily follow up with the stun from Pyke E Phantom Undertow, so keep your distance. When Pyke E Phantom Undertow starts, move sideways from the direction Pyke came from to avoid the stun. If you see a shark shadow beneath you while Pyke W Ghostwater Dive is active, retreat toward your allies or under your turret.

Rakan.build: Rakan starts fights with Rakan W Grand Entrance and Rakan R The Quickness, so get a crowd control cleanse first. If you build resistance, choose magic resistance to counter Rakan’s ability damage.
Rakan.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Rakan’s path to slow him, then hit him with Swain E Nevermove to root him. Recast E to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. When fighting with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, catch him with E and recast R after draining and healing enough.
Rakan.escape: Immediately after sidestepping Rakan W Grand Entrance, you have a window to counter with Swain E Nevermove. If Rakan is separated from his allies, he can’t use Rakan E Battle Dance to dash to them, so look for a chance to catch him then.
Rakan.fight: Trade immediately after the shield from Rakan P Fey Feathers is stripped away.
Rakan.laning: Keep your distance early and focus on avoiding Rakan W Grand Entrance. Pressure Rakan with Swain E Nevermove, but don’t push while E is down. When the enemy ADC steps up to last-hit, use Swain Q Death’s Hand to poke them along with the wave.
Rakan.phase: Swain lacks mana and an escape early, so survive by avoiding Rakan’s engage. Swain gains health as he collects soul fragments, so if you avoid falling far behind early, you’ll have an advantage later.
Rakan.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch Rakan with Swain E Nevermove right after he lands from Rakan W Grand Entrance. Stop him with E before Rakan R The Quickness reaches you, and don’t stand in line with an ally. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy moves in as a group and you can hit multiple targets.
Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance knocks you up at the landing spot after his dash, so sidestep when he starts moving. When Rakan R The Quickness is active, stop him with Swain E Nevermove before he touches you, and don’t stand in line with an ally.

Rell.build: Swain has no escape and is vulnerable to follow-up damage if caught by Rell’s crowd control, so consider prioritizing tenacity. If you build resistance, choose magic resistance over armor, while accounting for Rell P Break the Mold reducing that resistance and Rell E Full Tilt dealing damage based on your maximum health.
Rell.combo: If Rell’s mobility ability is down, place Swain W Vision of Empire in her path to slow her, then hit her with Swain E Nevermove to root her. Recast E to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you have a way to catch her, and recast it after draining and healing enough.
Rell.escape: Don’t engage just because Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down is down. You have a chance to catch her with Swain E Nevermove once Rell E Full Tilt is also down and before it comes back.
Rell.fight: Stay outside the range of Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down while she is mounted. Back away immediately after Rell uses Crash Down, then fight by catching her with Swain E Nevermove while Rell E Full Tilt is also down.
Rell.laning: Early on, pressure Rell with Swain E Nevermove from maximum range, outside her engage range. Rell has low magic resistance early and can’t recover health in lane, so use Swain Q Death’s Hand to hit her along with the wave and chip away at her health. Don’t push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Rell.phase: Swain is mana-starved early, so avoid repeated trades and manage your distance from Rell’s engage. Survive early while collecting soul fragments, and Swain will gain an advantage as the game goes on.
Rell.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull an enemy in with Swain E Nevermove. Keep your distance from allies before Rell engages so Rell R Magnet Storm can’t pull several of you together. When Rell and her team move in as a group, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension from a position where it can hit multiple targets.
Rell.watch: If Rell E Full Tilt speeds up Rell and one of her allies, that signals an engage. Stop trading and move out of the short range of Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down. Rell Q Shattering Strike travels in a straight line, so sidestep it.

Renata.build: Get a crowd control cleanse first against Renata Glasc Q Handshake and R Hostile Takeover. Build magic resistance to counter Renata Glasc’s magic damage. Renata Glasc P Leverage scales with maximum health, so be wary of relying on stacking health alone.
Renata.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Renata Glasc’s path, then hit the slowed target with Swain E Nevermove at maximum range. Recast E to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. When fighting with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, catch her with E, drain and heal, then recast R.
Renata.escape: You have an opening to engage after Renata Glasc Q Handshake and R Hostile Takeover are down. Renata Glasc has no mobility ability of her own, so if you hit her with Swain E Nevermove and close the distance, you can keep her caught. If Swain E is down, don’t activate Swain R Demonic Ascension first and chase her.
Renata.fight: Target Renata Glasc after Renata Glasc Q Handshake or R Hostile Takeover is down. Place Swain W Vision of Empire in her path to slow her, then catch her with Swain E Nevermove and hit her with Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you can catch her with E and have a target to drain.
Renata.laning: Avoid forcing repeated fights early because you’re mana-starved. Pressure Renata Glasc with Swain E Nevermove, but don’t push while E is down. Maintain lane pressure and build soul fragments by hitting champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and E.
Renata.phase: Swain is mana-starved early, so survive without taking a major disadvantage. As soul fragments build up your health, the game becomes more favorable for Swain later on.
Renata.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove. If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available, keep your distance from allies. When the enemy moves in as a group, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension from a position where it can hit multiple targets. Immediately after killing an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, retreat so your allies don’t die to the revived enemy.
Renata.watch: Renata Glasc Q Handshake roots the first target it hits, so stay behind minions or your frontline to avoid it. Don’t engage while grouped with allies when Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available. If you kill an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, retreat with your allies so that enemy can’t participate in a takedown and revive.

Senna.build: Senna’s main damage is physical, and Swain has relatively low armor, so build armor first. Buy Cloth Armor early and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots.
Senna.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Senna’s path to slow her, then root her with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in, and use Swain Q Death’s Hand when she is close. When fighting with Swain R Demonic Ascension, pull her in, then get as much drain and healing as possible before using the final attack.
Senna.escape: The window to close the distance is after Senna W Last Embrace is blocked by a minion or misses. Senna has no ability to create distance on her own, so once you get close, catch her with Swain E Nevermove.
Senna.fight: Watch where Senna steps forward to collect a soul and place Swain W Vision of Empire on her path ahead of time. Hit the slowed Senna with Swain E Nevermove and pull her in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when Swain E Nevermove or an ally’s crowd control can keep Senna in place.
Senna.laning: When the opponent steps forward to last-hit, use Swain Q Death’s Hand to hit both the wave and the opponent. Pressure with Swain E Nevermove, but do not push the wave while the ability is down.
Senna.phase: Senna has very little health early, giving you chances to disrupt her soul collection, but Swain lacks mana, so avoid forcing repeated fights. If you avoid falling far behind early and stack soul fragments, Swain’s health increases and he becomes more favored as the game goes on.
Senna.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline and catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove to pull them in. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the opponents move in as a group and it can reach multiple targets.
Senna.watch: Senna Q Piercing Darkness passes through allies and minions, so move out of the line between Senna and her target. Dodge Senna W Last Embrace from behind minions, and if it marks you, move away from allies before the root spreads. If Senna hits you once, back off so she cannot land a second attack and collect Mist.

Seraphine.build: The damage from Seraphine P Stage Presence, Q High Note, and E Beat Drop is all magic, so build magic resistance first. According to the available information, Seraphine has no resistance reduction or true damage, so the magic resistance you build remains effective throughout.
Seraphine.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Seraphine’s path first to slow her, then hit her with Swain E Nevermove and recast it to pull her in. Follow up with Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range, overlapping multiple bolts.
Seraphine.escape: Go in after letting Seraphine E Beat Drop pass without hitting you. Seraphine has no mobility ability, so if you catch her with Swain E Nevermove, pull her in and follow up with a close-range fight.
Seraphine.fight: The moment after dodging Seraphine E Beat Drop is a chance to engage. When Seraphine is alone and separated from her ADC, place Swain W Vision of Empire on her path and hit the slowed Seraphine with Swain E Nevermove to close the distance.
Seraphine.laning: Avoid forcing repeated fights early, and use Swain E Nevermove to pressure Seraphine as she approaches the wave. Do not push while Swain E Nevermove is down, and use Swain W Vision of Empire to hit a champion or check vision.
Seraphine.phase: Swain lacks mana early, making repeated fights difficult, so focus on avoiding a major deficit. His maximum health increases as soul fragments stack, so Swain becomes more favored as the game goes on.
Seraphine.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline and pull someone in with Swain E Nevermove. Spread out to the sides so Seraphine R Encore cannot extend through your allies. Use Swain R Demonic Ascension when the opponents move in as a group, it can hit multiple enemies, and you have a way to catch them.
Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots slowed enemies and stuns immobilized ones. If you are slowed, immediately move out of the line in front of Seraphine. Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it hits an ally, so do not line up with your allies in teamfights.

Sona.build: Sona’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. Make sure your team has at least one Grievous Wounds item to counter her late-game healing, and consider Morellonomicon on Swain.
Sona.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Sona’s path ahead of time to slow her, then hit her with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in and use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range.
Sona.escape: Engage when you can root Sona with Swain E Nevermove before Sona E Song of Celerity lets her create distance. After Sona R Crescendo is down, look for a chance to close the distance without needing to dodge its stun.
Sona.fight: From early on, force trades when Sona steps forward to use her aura, making her spend mana on healing. Sona sped up by Sona E Song of Celerity is hard to catch with slows alone, so look for an angle to hit her with Swain E Nevermove before going in.
Sona.laning: Land Swain E Nevermove to pressure Sona’s duo so they cannot approach the wave. Do not push while Swain E Nevermove is down, and use Swain Q Death’s Hand to hit both the wave and the opponent when they step forward to last-hit.
Sona.phase: In the late game, watch out for Sona’s scaling and team healing, but Swain also gains health from soul fragments and retains his value.
Sona.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline and use Swain E Nevermove to pull Sona out of the allied group, disrupting the positions where her aura can reach. If the opponents group up and come in, activate Swain R Demonic Ascension where it can hit multiple enemies, get enough drain and healing, then recast it.
Sona.watch: Sona’s basic attack empowered by Sona P Power Chord can deal bonus damage or slow you, so create distance if Sona suddenly steps into attack range. Sona R Crescendo stuns enemies in a line, so spread out to the sides from your allies when Sona steps forward.

Soraka.build: Soraka Q Starcall and Soraka E Equinox deal magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If fights last long enough that you have to deal with Soraka’s healing multiple times, consider Grievous Wounds next.
Soraka.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Soraka’s path first, then hit the slowed Soraka with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. In fights with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, get enough drain and healing before recasting it.
Soraka.escape: Engage once you see that Soraka E Equinox was used to poke and is down. Soraka has no mobility ability, so limit her path with Swain W Vision of Empire and catch her with Swain E Nevermove. If Soraka E Equinox’s zone is already placed, use your engage ability before entering it.
Soraka.fight: The moment Soraka E Equinox is down is a chance to engage. Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Soraka’s path ahead of time to slow her, then catch her with Swain E Nevermove, pull her in, and use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range.
Soraka.laning: Early on, avoid major losses while hitting Soraka with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to stack growth. Pressure Soraka’s allied ADC to make her use Soraka W Astral Infusion, but dodge Soraka Q Starcall so her health continues to drain. Do not push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Soraka.phase: Swain lacks mana early, so avoid repeated fights and focus on holding on without taking major losses. The more Swain P Ravenous Flock growth stacks you gain, the more favored you become as the game goes on.
Soraka.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline and look for a chance to catch Soraka with Swain E Nevermove. Focus your damage on Soraka herself rather than repeatedly hitting an ally who is being healed. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the opponents group up and come in and multiple enemies are in range.
Soraka.watch: If Soraka Q Starcall hits you, Soraka heals and gains movement speed, so dodge it while pressuring her. You are silenced within Soraka E Equinox’s zone and may also be rooted, so use your engage ability before stepping into the zone. Soraka R Wish heals her allies, so concentrate your damage into a short window.

Taric.build: The available information is not enough to determine the first purchase. Taric P Bravado and Taric E Dazzle deal magic damage, so build magic resistance if you need resistance.
Taric.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on the opponent’s path ahead of time to slow them, then root them with Swain E Nevermove. Recast E to pull them in and land Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. If Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity is active, hold the target with E and deal damage after the immunity ends.
Taric.escape: The moment after dodging the stun from Taric E Dazzle is a chance to engage. Taric has no ability to create distance on his own, so if you catch him with Swain E Nevermove, it is difficult for him to escape.
Taric.fight: Early on, do not take close-range fights while getting hit by Taric P Bravado’s empowered basic attacks. Dodge Taric E Dazzle to the side, then engage with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove after its stun is down. Use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range after pulling the target in.
Taric.laning: Look to land Swain E Nevermove from maximum range to pressure Taric’s side and keep them from approaching the wave. Do not push while E is down, and use Swain Q Death’s Hand to hit both the wave and the opponent stepping up to last-hit. Hit champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and E to stack soul fragments.
Taric.phase: Early on, watch out for Taric P Bravado’s close-range damage and conserve Swain’s mana while fighting. If you avoid falling far behind early and stack soul fragments, Swain becomes more favored as the game goes on.
Taric.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline, catch someone with Swain E Nevermove, and activate Swain R Demonic Ascension where it can hit multiple enemies when the opponents group up and come in. If you see the cast animation for Taric R Cosmic Radiance, decide whether to back away or pick off the enemy damage dealer. While damage immunity is active, hold the opponent with E and deal damage again as soon as it ends.
Taric.watch: If you see the tell for Taric E Dazzle, move sideways to dodge it. Do not unload damage while Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity is active.

Thresh.build: Swain has no ability to escape on his own, so prioritize tenacity against Thresh Q Death Sentence and Thresh E Flay. Build magic resistance rather than armor to resist damage from Thresh’s abilities.
Thresh.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Thresh’s path first to slow him, then hit him with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull him in and use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range.
Thresh.escape: The moment after dodging Thresh Q Death Sentence is a chance to close the distance. When Thresh W Dark Passage is also down, hitting him with Swain E Nevermove makes it difficult for him to escape. If Thresh E Flay is still available, avoid positions where it can pull you in.
Thresh.fight: Dodge Thresh Q Death Sentence to the side, then close the distance. Once Thresh W Dark Passage is also down, slow his path with Swain W Vision of Empire and catch him with Swain E Nevermove.
Thresh.laning: Early on, watch for Thresh’s repeated engages and keep your distance; trade when he steps forward to collect souls. After leveling up Swain Q Death’s Hand, hit both the wave and the opposing ADC when they step forward to last-hit. Do not push while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Thresh.phase: Early on, Swain lacks mana for repeated fights, and getting caught by Thresh makes it easy to take follow-up hits, so hold on and manage your distance. Swain’s value grows in the late game as soul fragments increase his health, so it is important not to fall far behind early.
Thresh.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline, catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove, and activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the opponents group up and come in. If Thresh W Dark Passage appears, finish off the target immediately or back away. If you are trapped in Thresh R The Box, choose a direction with your allies to break out.
Thresh.watch: If Thresh Q Death Sentence hits you, Thresh can dash in and follow up with Thresh E Flay, so move sideways when you see the hook windup. Also avoid standing in the line between Thresh and an ally to reduce the chance of being pulled in by Thresh E Flay.

Velkoz.build: Build movement speed first so you can get out of the telegraphed attack areas. Magic resistance helps against Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission, W Void Rift, and E Tectonic Disruption. Resistance cannot stop the true damage from Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction and R Life Form Disintegration Ray, so build health as well.
Velkoz.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Vel’Koz’s path ahead of time, then hit the slowed Vel’Koz with Swain E Nevermove. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull him in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. In fights with Swain R Demonic Ascension active, get enough drain and healing before recasting it.
Velkoz.escape: The moment after Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption misses is a chance to engage. Vel’Koz has no mobility ability, so if you catch him with Swain E Nevermove then, it is difficult for him to create distance again. When dodging Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission, do not just move sideways; get out of the split beam’s path before engaging.
Velkoz.fight: Close the distance after Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption misses. Place Swain W Vision of Empire on his path to slow him, then catch and pull him in with Swain E Nevermove, followed by Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. If you get very close, Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption can knock you back, so do not rush in while it is available.
Velkoz.laning: Early on, you lack the mana for repeated fights, so endure Vel’Koz’s poke and dodge it. Pressure him by hitting Swain E Nevermove from maximum range, and do not push while it misses or is down. Use Swain W Vision of Empire to hit Vel’Koz or check vision in the river and tri-brush rather than hitting minions.
Velkoz.phase: Early on, Swain lacks mana, so focus on avoiding major losses. In the late game, Swain’s value increases thanks to the health stacked through Swain P Ravenous Flock.
Velkoz.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline and look for a chance to pull Vel’Koz in with Swain E Nevermove. When Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray starts, prioritize interrupting it with the forced movement from Swain E Nevermove. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the opponents group up and come in and multiple enemies are in range, then get enough drain and healing before recasting it.
Velkoz.watch: Dodge not only the initial beam from Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission but also its split beams. Do not just move sideways; move toward Vel’Koz or behind where the beam passed. If you are hit by abilities in quick succession, Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction triggers true damage, so back away and let the stacks wear off when you have them. Prioritize interrupting Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray with Swain E Nevermove as soon as it starts.

Xerath.build: First, get a way to cleanse or remove the stun from Xerath E Shocking Orb. Xerath’s damage is magic, so build magic resistance afterward, and also get movement speed to leave telegraphed attack areas.
Xerath.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire on Xerath’s path ahead of time to slow him, then hit him with Swain E Nevermove from maximum range. Recast Swain E Nevermove to pull him in and land Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. If you activate Swain R Demonic Ascension, keep draining the opponent and healing; once Swain R Demonic Ascension is available again, use it.
Xerath.escape: The moment after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down is a chance to engage. Xerath has no mobility ability, so close the distance then and catch him with Swain E Nevermove. Xerath cannot move while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so you can engage on him there.
Xerath.fight: Close the distance right after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. While Xerath charges Xerath Q Arcanopulse, dodge sideways as you approach, then, after catching him, land Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range.
Xerath.laning: Early on, farm while avoiding Xerath’s heavy damage, then push the wave and call your jungler when Xerath runs out of mana. Pressure the opponent’s approach to the wave by hitting Swain E Nevermove, but do not push while Swain E Nevermove is down. Hit champions with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to stack soul fragments.
Xerath.phase: Early on, focus on enduring Xerath’s long range without falling far behind. In the late game, Swain becomes more favored thanks to the growth he gains from Swain P Ravenous Flock and soul fragments.
Xerath.teamfight: Stand just behind your allied frontline and catch an enemy with Swain E Nevermove to pull them in. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension and keep draining and healing when the opponents group up and multiple enemies are in range. When you see the cast animation for Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, dodge the attack or, if you can engage, target Xerath while he cannot move.
Xerath.watch: Xerath Q Arcanopulse passes through minions, so when you see him charging, change direction and dodge to the side. Watch for the slow from Xerath W Eye of Destruction and the stun from Xerath E Shocking Orb, especially to avoid being stunned and taking successive follow-up attacks. Start dodging immediately when you see the cast animation for Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.

Zilean.build: Build tenacity first to prepare for being caught by Zilean Q Time Bomb’s stun and slowed by Zilean E Time Warp. Zilean deals magic damage, so build magic resistance when adding defenses.
Zilean.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Zilean’s path to slow him, then hit Swain E Nevermove from maximum range. Recast E to pull him in and hit Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range.
Zilean.escape: Engage after Zilean Q Time Bomb and W Rewind’s combo, and Zilean E Time Warp, are down. Zilean has no mobility spell, so catch him with Swain E Nevermove during that window.
Zilean.laning: Hit Zilean with Swain W Vision of Empire and Swain E Nevermove to collect Soul Fragments and pressure him as he approaches the wave. Don’t push the lane while Swain E Nevermove is down.
Zilean.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and pull one enemy in with Swain E Nevermove. When the enemy team groups up and comes in so that Swain R Demonic Ascension can reach multiple enemies, activate it and keep draining and healing. If Zilean R Chronoshift is on an enemy targeting your carries, switch your target to Zilean himself.
Zilean.watch: If Zilean Q Time Bomb attaches to you, move away from your allies and get outside its blast radius.

Zyra.build: Zyra deals magic damage, so build magic resistance for defenses. However, if Swain is caught by Zyra E Grasping Roots and R Stranglethorns and taking plant damage, consider tenacity first. Movement speed is also useful for walking out of telegraphed areas.
Zyra.combo: Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Zyra’s path first, then hit the slowed Zyra with Swain E Nevermove. Recast E to pull her in, then use Swain Q Death’s Hand at close range. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when you can keep draining by catching a target with E, then recast it after you’ve healed enough.
Zyra.escape: The moment after you dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots is your chance to engage. Zyra has no skill to create distance herself, so close in and catch her with Swain E Nevermove. If you see the indicator for Zyra R Stranglethorns, don’t continue the engage; walk out of its area.
Zyra.fight: Dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots by moving sideways, then close the distance when there are no plants nearby. Place Swain W Vision of Empire in Zyra’s path ahead of time to slow her, then hit Swain E Nevermove. Don’t take a fight in an area where Zyra’s plants have been established for a while.
Zyra.laning: Early on, manage your distance to avoid Zyra E Grasping Roots while collecting Soul Fragments. Step on seeds when it’s safe, but back off when Zyra uses a spell, then approach again. Pressure Zyra with Swain E Nevermove, but don’t push the lane while E is down.
Zyra.phase: Early on, Swain lacks mana and escape options, so focus on avoiding a heavy loss while dodging Zyra E Grasping Roots. Your health increases as you collect Soul Fragments, so surviving the early game puts you in a better position later.
Zyra.teamfight: Stand just behind your frontline and catch one enemy with Swain E Nevermove, recasting it when the pull destination is favorable. Don’t fight where Zyra has accumulated seeds; move the fight elsewhere. Activate Swain R Demonic Ascension when the enemy team groups up and comes in and you can keep it on several enemies.
Zyra.watch: If Zyra E Grasping Roots catches Swain, his lack of an escape ability makes it difficult to avoid the follow-up damage. Dodge the straight-line E by moving sideways at the edge of its range. When you see the summon indicator for Zyra R Stranglethorns, walk out of its area before it knocks you up. Don’t fight where her plants are clustered; briefly back off.
